name: Nevada

law.name: Revised Uniform Athlete Agents Act (NRS chapter 398A)

covers_nil_agents: Yes. An agency contract includes endorsement contracts (NRS 398A.020). Nevada's NIL law lets athletes use an agent registered under NRS 398A (NRS 398.300).
summary: Register with the Secretary of State. $500.

steps.text: Fill out the Nevada athlete agent application

steps.detail: Same fee if you use another state's registration.

steps.text: Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director in writing before you first contact the athlete
steps.detail: This also applies before you ask someone else to talk to the athlete for you. If the athlete reached out first, tell the athletic director within 10 days.

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Say you are registered in Nevada and list your other states. Add your pay and how it's figured, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed.

steps.text: Put the warning to the student athlete in bold, right above their signature
steps.detail: Use the exact words the law gives. If the athlete is a minor, a parent or guardian signs and the warning is reworded for them.

steps.text: Have the athlete sign a separate eligibility warning
steps.detail: It says signing may cost them their eligibility. A parent or guardian signs instead if the athlete is a minor.

steps.text: Give the athlete a copy of the contract and the signed warning when they sign
Tell the athletic director in writing within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, whichever comes first. The athlete may cancel within 14 days.

steps.text: If the athlete enrolls at a school later, tell that athletic director within 72 hours
steps.detail: The clock starts when you knew or should have known they enrolled.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: State law and federal law (SPARTA) both ban pre-dating or post-dating it.
Names and addresses of your athletes, every contract and what you spent to recruit each one. The Secretary of State can inspect them.

steps.text: Never make false promises or give gifts that could cost an athlete eligibility
steps.detail: A gift is only allowed if you tell the athletic director within 72 hours and the athlete signs that they know the risk. Breaking these rules can mean jail and a fine up to $50,000.
Your registration lasts 2 years. Renewal is also $500.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: The Secretary of State's forms page could not be read. Confirm the form name and how to file at nvsos.gov/licensing/sports-agents.

The $500 fees come from NAC 398.100, a 2001 rule written for the old athlete agent law. It is still in the current code, but confirm with the Secretary of State that it still applies under NRS 398A.270.
contract_warning: Warning to student athlete. If you sign this contract: (a) you may lose your eligibility to compete as a student athlete in your sport; (b) if you have an athletic director, within 72 hours after signing this contract or before the next scheduled athletic event in which you participate, whichever occurs first, both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director that you have entered into this contract and provide the name and contact information of the athlete agent; and (c) you may cancel this contract within 14 days after signing it. Cancellation of this contract may not reinstate your eligibility as a student athlete in your sport.
